items.text: When a claim contradicts what I already believed, I look into it rather than dismissing it.
I enjoy testing my own ideas against people who see things differently.
In the last month, a source felt right mainly because it was new or original.
I can hold a question open for days without needing it settled now.
Before sharing something important, I check it, every time, even when I am in a hurry.
I finish verification steps I start, rather than stopping halfway.
In the last month, I shared or forwarded something I meant to check and did not.
I keep track of where my important claims came from.
When I find something striking, I want to tell people about it quickly.
I am usually the one who passes on news to my groups.
In the last month, I posted something before I had checked it.
Talking through a decision with others matters more to me than deciding alone.
When someone I deal with is insistent, I tend to go along rather than push back.
I find it hard to say no directly, so I soften it until the no is unclear.
I give people the benefit of the doubt by default.
In the last month, I agreed to something to avoid an awkward conversation.
When something upsets me online, I can wait before reacting.
Strong news in the last month moved me to act faster than I later thought wise.
When I am stressed, decisions that would normally take minutes get made in seconds.
Being criticized does not usually change what I believe about the facts.
If I get an unexpected benefit from a deal, I check what the other side gets out of it.
When someone does me a favor, I feel I owe them one even if I never asked for it.
I am comfortable returning something or refusing a gift that came with strings.
Terms that favor me by someone else's mistake get flagged, not pocketed.
A deadline appearing suddenly makes me decide before I would otherwise.
"Last chance" framing has moved me in the last month.
Official-looking format — letterhead, form numbers, titles — makes a claim easier for me to accept.
I have followed an instruction because of who it appeared to come from, without checking the channel.
Finding out everyone around me agrees on something makes me less likely to examine it.
The idea of being out of step with a group I value bothers me more than being wrong does.
Believing something may run out or be withdrawn makes me decide faster than I should.
Seeing others get something I have not gotten yet makes me move before I have checked it.
When a conversation turns sharp, I concede points I would normally defend.
After a conflict, I give in just to make it end, and regret it later.
Someone asking me to keep something between us has made me feel singled out and special.
I have gone along with something partly because no one else was there to see it.
Late at night or exhausted, I approve, buy, or agree to things I would not in the morning.
When I am worn down, long messages get answered on tone rather than content.
